note: Two independent complete General Relativity lecture-note treatments and one specialized complete paper were inspected at the recorded locators. Their conventions are compared, not silently imported; every harvested result has a scoped disposition. The unassigned Harte WKB source belongs to later ML05 work and is not used for this page. The C2 curve-acceleration extension was separately defined and proved on emg-mm01; Tong §§3.2.1–3.2.3 and Carroll Ch. 3 were inspected for the coordinate connection formulas, with C2 overlap invariance proved locally. All three sources fetch-verify; no retrieval failure, recovery search, dropped source, or source-resolution escalation occurred. The prior emg-mg04 authoring hold has current ready-for-authoring records at the owner-bound sources, as detailed in the batch dependency evidence.

sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019, complete author-hosted lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 290-page PDF inspected. Sections 4.5.3–4.5.5, PDF pp. 190–196 (printed pp. 183–189), and §4.5.7, PDF pp. 201–204 (printed pp. 194–197).

contents.name: §4.5.3, equation (4.52): metric Maxwell tensor and flat-frame energy density

source_review.read_extent: The complete 290-page PDF was inspected at the full metric-variation paragraph and displayed Maxwell tensor, including the stated F-component convention and flat-frame T00 formula.
source_review.supports: Supports the tensor formula and component convention. Tong sets c=1; the local definition states SI units and its later component theorem independently expands the tensor, so no source normalization or proof is imported.

contents.name: §4.5.4, equations (4.53)–(4.55): perfect-fluid tensor and energy/Euler projections

source_review.read_extent: The complete 290-page PDF was inspected through the rest-frame tensor, its covariant form, and the two balance projections.
source_review.supports: Supports the perfect-fluid rest-frame and covariant tensor conventions. The consumer proof directly redoes the projection for an explicit Lorentz-force density and adds only the separately stated Ohmic current hypothesis.

contents.name: §4.5.7, equations (4.60)–(4.62): WEC, SEC, NEC and DEC vocabulary

source_review.read_extent: The complete energy-conditions section was inspected through the definitions and its perfect-fluid WEC/SEC/NEC/DEC checks.
source_review.supports: Supports the pointwise vocabulary and standard perfect-fluid inequalities. Tong writes SEC as a curvature condition and invokes Einstein's equation; the local definition instead specifies the trace-reversed tensor inequality without that physical premise.

contents.name: §4.5.7, perfect-fluid energy-condition limits and the dominant inequality

source_review.read_extent: The complete relevant pages were inspected, including the boosted-observer WEC/SEC discussion and the DEC current and |p| bound.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent check on the claimed perfect-fluid ranges. The item derives the exact iff conditions directly in its fixed signature and does not import Tong's curvature/Einstein inference for SEC.

contents.name: §4.5.5, finite-region current balance, side flux and Killing stress current

source_review.read_extent: The complete 4.5.5 discussion was inspected through the curved divergence theorem, the side-boundary condition, and the Killing-generated current.
source_review.supports: Supports the need to retain side flux and the Killing-current construction. The item states an exact finite singular-chain convention and proves its own index sign from its conditional Maxwell and matter identities.

contents.name: §3.2.1 covariant differentiation and §3.2.3 Levi-Civita connection: coordinate formula extended to a C² curve

source_review.read_extent: The complete 290-page author-hosted PDF was opened and the full relevant coordinate-connection and Levi-Civita passages were inspected.
source_review.supports: Supports the local coordinate formula for covariant differentiation and the metric-selected connection. The C² regularity extension is checked locally using the current connection-matrix transformation law; no source proof of that extension is claimed.

sources.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), complete PDF
sources.locator: Complete 238-page PDF inspected. §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.111), PDF pp. 35–37 (printed pp. 28–31); Ch. 5, equations (5.41)–(5.43), PDF pp. 147–148 (printed pp. 140–141).

contents.name: §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.106): dust number current and stress tensor

source_review.read_extent: The full equations and surrounding dust discussion in the complete PDF were read, including the rest-frame number density and covariant dust tensor.
source_review.supports: Supports the dust tensor interpretation. Carroll uses c=1; the local definition specifies SI normalization and does not infer the charged exchange equation from Carroll.

contents.name: §1.4.1, equations (1.107)–(1.110): perfect-fluid rest tensor and covariant form

source_review.read_extent: The full displayed rest-frame tensor and the algebra leading to its covariant form were inspected in the complete PDF.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent treatment of the perfect-fluid tensor. The local item carries the c factors and unit assignments explicitly.

source_review.read_extent: The displayed Maxwell stress tensor and its adjacent convention text were inspected.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent tensor-form comparison. Carroll uses Gaussian units and a different normalization; the consumer proof recomputes the SI components locally.

contents.name: Ch. 5, equations (5.41)–(5.43): Killing equation and uncharged geodesic first integral

source_review.read_extent: The full local Killing-vector argument and derivative of the geodesic contraction were read in the complete PDF.
source_review.supports: Supports the uncharged comparison only. The local item independently proves the stress current and charged gauge-compensated first integral, including its sign and local-potential hypothesis.

contents.name: Ch. 3 covariant derivative and connection coefficients, equations (3.1), (3.12)–(3.14): independent coordinate treatment

source_review.read_extent: The complete 238-page PDF was opened and the relevant coordinate formulas and surrounding discussion were inspected.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent coordinate expression for covariant derivatives and explains the non-tensorial transformation of connection coefficients. The local proof verifies the resulting acceleration transforms as a vector for C² curves.
